subject: english-literature
title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9-1) English Literature 4ET1

papers.name: Paper 1: Poetry and Modern Prose
papers.materials: A clean copy of the anthology poems is provided for use with Section B.
instructions: Use black ink or ball-point pen.
Answer THREE questions: the question in Section A, ONE question from Section B and ONE question from Section C.
Write your answers in the spaces provided; you may not need all the space.
Copies of the set texts and of the anthology may not be brought into the examination.
information: The total mark for this paper is 90.
The number of marks for each question is shown in brackets: use it as a guide to timing.
Section A is worth 20 marks, Section B 30 marks and Section C 40 marks.
advice: Read each question carefully before you start to write.
Plan your time: about 35 minutes for Section A, 40 for Section B and 45 for Section C.
Check your answers if you have time at the end.

sections.title: SECTION A: Unseen Poetry
sections.instructions: Answer the question in this section. You should spend 35 minutes on this question.

sections.title: SECTION B: Anthology Poetry
sections.instructions: Answer ONE question from this section. You should spend 40 minutes on your chosen question.

sections.title: SECTION C: Modern Prose - Of Mice and Men, John Steinbeck
sections.instructions: Answer ONE question from this section. You should spend 45 minutes on this section.

qtypes.label: Unseen poem essay
qtypes.description: Explore how the writer presents a given focus in a poem printed on the paper (AO2).

qtypes.label: Anthology comparison: two named poems
qtypes.description: Compare how two named anthology poems present a theme (AO2 + AO3).

qtypes.label: Anthology comparison: one named poem + one of your choice
qtypes.description: Compare a named anthology poem with another poem you choose (AO2 + AO3).

qtypes.label: Of Mice and Men: character essay
qtypes.description: Essay on a character or relationship, with context (AO1 + AO4).

qtypes.label: Of Mice and Men: theme or methods essay
qtypes.description: Essay on a theme, setting or Steinbeck's methods, with context (AO1 + AO4).

subtopics.title: Nature, seasons and the natural world
subtopics.summary: Unseen poems about landscapes, weather, plants, animals and the seasons.

points.summary: Explain how imagery and description bring a natural scene to life.
Show how a poet uses nature to suggest feelings or ideas.

subtopics.title: Family, childhood and growing up
subtopics.summary: Unseen poems about parents, grandparents, siblings and childhood experiences.

points.summary: Analyse how a poet presents a relationship between family members.
Comment on how a child's point of view or growing up is shown.

subtopics.title: Memory, time and change
subtopics.summary: Unseen poems that look back, reflect on ageing or show how time changes things.

points.summary: Explain how structure and tense shifts move between past and present.
Analyse how a poet presents the effects of time.

subtopics.title: Places, journeys and home
subtopics.summary: Unseen poems about cities, homes, journeys and being away from home.

points.summary: Analyse how a poet creates a sense of place.
Comment on how a journey or a home is given wider meaning.

subtopics.title: Love, loss and strong feelings
subtopics.summary: Unseen poems expressing joy, grief, fear, hope, loneliness or love.

points.summary: Explain how language choices convey strong emotion.
Analyse how form and structure shape a poem's emotional effect.

subtopics.title: People, society and the wider world
subtopics.summary: Unseen poems about communities, work, war, power and freedom.

points.summary: Analyse how a poet presents a community or a social issue.
Comment on the poet's attitude and how it is conveyed.

subtopics.title: Identity, culture and language
subtopics.summary: Comparing poems about who we are: culture, language, heritage and belonging.

subtopics.title: Love and relationships
subtopics.summary: Comparing poems about love, marriage, family bonds and controlling relationships.

points.summary: La Belle Dame sans Merci (John Keats)
Do not go gentle into that good night (Dylan Thomas)

subtopics.title: Death, loss and grief
subtopics.summary: Comparing poems about dying, mourning, loss and how people respond to death.

points.summary: Do not go gentle into that good night (Dylan Thomas)
La Belle Dame sans Merci (John Keats)

subtopics.title: Childhood, memory and time
subtopics.summary: Comparing poems that look back to childhood or reflect on the passing of time.

subtopics.title: Power, control and conflict
subtopics.summary: Comparing poems about power, control, conflict and those who hold or resist it.

points.summary: La Belle Dame sans Merci (John Keats)

subtopics.title: Advice, attitudes and strong points of view
subtopics.summary: Comparing poems with a strong persuasive voice giving advice or arguing a view.

points.summary: Do not go gentle into that good night (Dylan Thomas)

subtopics.title: Experience, suffering and the wider world
subtopics.summary: Comparing poems that capture a vivid event, a moment, or the experience of suffering.

points.summary: La Belle Dame sans Merci (John Keats)

topics.title: Section C: Modern prose - Of Mice and Men

subtopics.title: George, Lennie and their friendship
subtopics.summary: The two central characters and the bond that sets them apart from other ranch workers.

points.summary: Know how George and Lennie are presented and how they change.
Explain why their friendship is unusual and how it ends.

subtopics.title: Curley and Curley's wife
subtopics.summary: The boss's son, his unnamed wife and their unhappy marriage.

points.summary: Explain how Curley's insecurity and aggression drive events.
Discuss how Curley's wife is presented as both threat and victim.

subtopics.title: Candy, Crooks and the outsiders
subtopics.summary: Characters pushed to the edge of ranch life by age, injury, race or gender.

points.summary: Know the roles of Candy and Crooks and the scene in Crooks's room.
Link each outsider to attitudes of the 1930s.

subtopics.title: Slim, Carlson and choosing a character
subtopics.summary: Other ranch workers and the 'which one character' style of question.

points.summary: Know the roles of Slim, Carlson, the boss and Whit.
Choose and justify one character against others.

subtopics.title: Dreams, money and happiness
subtopics.summary: The dream farm, other characters' hopes, wages and the American Dream.

points.summary: Explain how the dream is presented and why it fails.
Link the dream to the Depression and the American Dream.

subtopics.title: Loneliness, friendship and love
subtopics.summary: Isolation on the ranch and the rare relationships that resist it.

points.summary: Show how most characters are lonely and why.
Discuss the forms of friendship, loyalty and love in the novel.

subtopics.title: Power, prejudice and violence
subtopics.summary: Who holds power on the ranch, how outsiders are treated, and the novel's violence.

points.summary: Explain how power and respect work in the ranch hierarchy.
Discuss prejudice (race, gender, age, disability) and violence.

subtopics.title: Death, loss and fate
subtopics.summary: The chain of deaths, what characters lose, and the sense that the ending is inevitable.

points.summary: Trace the deaths and how each foreshadows the next.
Discuss fate, responsibility, guilt and memory.

subtopics.title: Setting, nature and structure
subtopics.summary: Steinbeck's methods: locations, animals, foreshadowing and the circular, play-like structure.

points.summary: Explain the importance of the pool, bunkhouse, Crooks's room and barn.
Analyse the use of animals, foreshadowing and structure.
